title: Add the owned-scope write regression test
description:
The highest-value test in the suite. Construct each of the 10 store-backed primitives inside a component body, drive the external producer (call maybeExecute / addItem / etc.), and assert no error is thrown and no console.error is emitted.

This is the regression for useSelector's ownedWrite: true — @tanstack/store notifies synchronously from set(), so the subscription callback inherits whatever scope the caller was in, and if that is a component body or an effect a plain write would throw REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE.

It is also what catches the create*Signal defect: mount createThrottledValue and createRateLimitedValue and assert they do not throw on first render (leading:true / immediate-execute-under-limit both write a plain signal from inside the effect half), plus createDebouncedValue with leading:true explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: All 10 primitives construct and fire inside a component body without throwing; the three create*Value wrappers mount cleanly including the leading-edge paths; the test fails against an unfixed build.

title: Convert the 3 create*Value effects to the two-arg split form
description:
createDebouncedValue, createRateLimitedValue and createThrottledValue each have:
  createEffect(() => { setV(value() as any) })

Solid 2's one-arg createEffect is removed. Convert to the split form with the reactive read in the TRACKED compute half and the write in the BRACED effect half:
  createEffect(() => value(), (next) => { setV(next as any) })

The discipline that makes this work: every reactive read goes in the compute half. A reactive value read in the effect half does not subscribe, producing a stale-update bug no type will catch.

The braces are mandatory (see the ESLint rule): an expression-bodied arrow leaks setV's return value into the cleanup slot and halts reactivity process-wide.

Note each also reads value() untracked at call time for the initial value; that is correct and stays.
acceptance_criteria: All three mirror their input accessor after a settle; the ESLint rule passes; a test asserts the mirror still updates on a second input change (the stale-subscription regression).

title: Fix owned-scope write in the 3 create*Signal wrappers
description:
THE non-obvious defect this port must fix.

createDebouncedSignal, createRateLimitedSignal and createThrottledSignal each do createSignal<TValue>(value) and hand instance.maybeExecute back as the setter. Their create*Value siblings then mirror an input accessor into that setter from inside an effect.

Throttler defaults leading: true, and RateLimiter executes immediately while under the limit. So maybeExecute executes SYNCHRONOUSLY inside the effect half and writes that plain signal from an owned scope, which is REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE — a hard dev-time throw in Solid 2. createThrottledValue therefore breaks on first render.

Debouncer defaults leading: false, so createDebouncedValue looks fine and breaks only with leading: true — which is exactly why this needs a regression test rather than a manual smoke check.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Complete the Solid 2 dependency bump (epic: toolchain) so packages/solid-pacer builds against solid-js 2.0.0-beta.30 in dev mode.
2. Mount examples/solid/createThrottledValue, or in a test render a component whose body calls createThrottledValue(someAccessor, { wait: 500 }).
3. On first render the mirror effect runs, calls maybeExecute, and the Throttler executes on the leading edge synchronously.
4. Observe the dev runtime throw REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE from the createSignal write inside createThrottledSignal.
5. Same via createRateLimitedValue (immediate execute while under the limit), and via createDebouncedValue when passed leading: true.

## Fix
1. Add { ownedWrite: true } to createSignal in all three create*Signal wrappers.
2. Solid 2's value overload takes Exclude<T, Function> (a bare function argument is reserved for the compute form), so the generic TValue needs the same cast the store repo uses in useSelector.ts.
3. Re-derive the 'instance.maybeExecute as Setter<TValue>' cast: Solid 2's Setter<in out T> is invariant and its overloads return U, while maybeExecute returns void.
acceptance_criteria: createThrottledValue and createRateLimitedValue mount without throwing; createDebouncedValue with leading:true likewise; all three compile with no as-unknown-as escape hatches beyond the documented Setter cast.

title: Replace the cleanup-only createEffect wrapper in the 10 store-backed primitives
description:
Identical change in createDebouncer, createThrottler, createBatcher, createQueuer, createRateLimiter and their five async twins.

Each currently has:
  createEffect(() => { onCleanup(() => { ...unmount... }) })

The one-arg createEffect is removed in Solid 2 (it types as never). Do NOT mechanically convert to the two-arg form — the wrapper existed only to scope the cleanup, and 'createEffect(() => {}, () => onCleanup(...))' would put a non-function return in the effect half and risk REACTIVITY_HALTED. onCleanup works directly in a component body, so just unwrap it.

Also in each file: move 'import type { Accessor, JSX } from solid-js' so JSX comes from @solidjs/web and Accessor stays on solid-js.

Leave completely alone: both useSelector calls, the 'shallow' import, and 'import type { Store }' — the migrated solid-store re-exports @tanstack/store, so those specifiers still resolve.
acceptance_criteria: All 10 files compile; no createEffect remains in them; each primitive's cleanup still fires on owner disposal.

title: Port PacerProvider to Solid 2 context-as-provider
description:
packages/solid-pacer/src/provider/PacerProvider.tsx is the only .tsx file and the only JSX site in src.

Changes: <PacerContext.Provider value={contextValue}> becomes <PacerContext value={contextValue}> (in Solid 2 the context object IS the provider); the closing tag likewise; and 'import type { JSX } from solid-js' becomes '@solidjs/web'.

Already correct and must not be changed: createContext<PacerContextValue | null>(null). Solid 2's createContext with no default makes useContext throw ContextNotFoundError; the explicit null default is the Solid-2-correct shape and useDefaultPacerOptions already handles null via '?? {}'.

Note for review: props.defaultOptions is read eagerly at construction, so provider options are snapshotted, not reactive. That is pre-existing Solid 1 behaviour — preserve it here rather than fixing it as a drive-by.
acceptance_criteria: Provider compiles under jsxImportSource @solidjs/web; a component under PacerProvider receives its defaultOptions; a component with no provider gets {} and does not throw.

title: Add the braced-effect-half ESLint rule
description:
Copy the no-restricted-syntax rule verbatim from /home/kaalin/dev/store/packages/solid-store/eslint.config.js into packages/solid-pacer/eslint.config.js, scoped to src/**.

Selector: CallExpression[callee.name=/^create(Render)?Effect$/][arguments.1.type='ArrowFunctionExpression'][arguments.1.body.type!='BlockStatement']

Why it matters: Solid 2 treats the effect half's return value as a cleanup slot. Any non-undefined, non-function value throws in dev and permanently halts the reactive system (REACTIVITY_HALTED) — silently, process-wide. An expression-bodied arrow leaks its expression's value into that slot, so 'createEffect(() => src(), v => results.push(v))' is fatal while the braced form is fine.

Land this FIRST so the rest of the epic is linted as it is written.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm test:eslint passes; an intentionally expression-bodied effect half is reported as an error.

title: Install and verify a single Solid 2 runtime
description:
node_modules is NOT currently installed in this repo, so this is a from-scratch resolve and the lockfile diff will be large.

Run pnpm install, then verify the graph rather than trusting it:
  pnpm why solid-js      -> 2.0.0-beta.30 for solid-pacer and its examples; 1.9.x ONLY under the devtools family
  pnpm why @solidjs/web  -> a single copy
  ls packages/solid-pacer/node_modules/@tanstack/solid-store/dist/index.js

Two Solid runtimes in one graph is the failure mode that matters here: it means two template caches and two event-delegation roots, undisposed cross-runtime computations, and (observed in the table repo's spike) a REACTIVITY_HALTED that kills the host app.
acceptance_criteria: All three verification commands give the expected result; pnpm-lock.yaml committed; no package resolves two solid-js majors into one importer.
close_reason: Verified: solid-pacer and all 26 examples resolve solid-js and @solidjs/web at exactly 2.0.0-beta.30; the devtools family resolves 1.9.13/1.9.14 with no Solid 2 anywhere in that subtree; the git-pinned @tanstack/solid-store unpacked with dist/ present and importable.

title: Update solid-pacer build and test config for vite-plugin-solid 3
description:
packages/solid-pacer/tsdown.config.ts and vitest.config.ts both import vite-plugin-solid; with the devDep bumped to 3.0.0-next.21 they pick it up automatically, but both need a verification pass because the plugin's behaviour changed.

vitest.config.ts also needs: uncomment setupFiles: ['./tests/test-setup.ts'] (line 12, currently commented out because the file never existed), and switch environment from happy-dom to jsdom to match the store repo's working Solid 2 harness.

Do NOT add resolve.conditions / ssr.resolve.conditions / server.deps.inline. Those are only needed WITHOUT the plugin — vite-plugin-solid 3 injects the browser/development conditions itself, including in test mode. The store repo's vitest.config.ts is 9 lines for exactly this reason.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm build produces dist for all 14 entry points and publint --strict passes; pnpm test:lib starts and picks up tests/.

title: Point solid-pacer tsconfig at the Solid 2 JSX runtime
description:
packages/solid-pacer/tsconfig.json: jsxImportSource from "solid-js" to "@solidjs/web" (jsx stays "preserve").

Also add customConditions: ["browser", "development"], mirroring /home/kaalin/dev/store/packages/solid-store/tsconfig.json. Without it, tsc type-checks against solid-js's inert server build (solid-js@2 maps the bare node condition to a server runtime where effects never run) while the tests execute the browser/development runtime that vite-plugin-solid injects. That mismatch produces type errors that do not correspond to anything real, and hides ones that do.

tsconfig.docs.json extends this file and needs no separate change.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm test:types passes for packages/solid-pacer against the Solid 2 typings.

title: Set Solid 2 peer and dev dependencies in packages/solid-pacer
description:
peerDependencies: solid-js and @solidjs/web both at ">=2.0.0-beta.30 <3.0.0". devDependencies: solid-js 2.0.0-beta.30, @solidjs/web 2.0.0-beta.30, vite-plugin-solid 3.0.0-next.21, @solidjs/testing-library 1.0.0-beta.2. Remove the solid-js ^1.9.12 devDep and the >=1.9.5 peer.

Two things learned the hard way and verified against npm:
- @solidjs/web must be a PEER, not a dependency. @solidjs/web@2.0.0-beta.30 peer-pins solid-js ^2.0.0-beta.30; they bump in lockstep and must never be bumped one alone. Shipping it as a regular dep risks two copies in one graph, which means two template caches and two event-delegation roots.
- A plain >=2.0.0 range does NOT match a beta. Semver admits a prerelease only when some comparator shares its major.minor.patch, so the -beta.30 suffix in the range is load-bearing.

The table and store repos pin the exact version (no caret) on the Solid 2 side because of beta churn.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm install resolves solid-js and @solidjs/web at exactly 2.0.0-beta.30 with no peer warnings for solid-pacer; publint --strict passes.

title: Pin @tanstack/solid-store to the store-repo commit hash
description:
In packages/solid-pacer/package.json dependencies, replace "@tanstack/solid-store": "^0.11.0" with the commit-pinned git spec:

  github:dkkloimwieder/store#<hash>&path:/packages/solid-store

CRITICAL: this pin must live in packages/solid-pacer/package.json ONLY. It must NOT go in pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides, because packages/pacer-devtools also depends on @tanstack/solid-store ^0.11.0 and is a Solid 1 app consumed by the React, Preact and Solid devtools adapters. A workspace override would redirect it onto the Solid 2 build and break three adapters at once.

The migrated solid-store still does 'export * from @tanstack/store', so shallow and the Store type keep resolving from the same specifier. None of the 20 useSelector call sites in solid-pacer need import changes.
acceptance_criteria: packages/solid-pacer/node_modules/@tanstack/solid-store/dist/index.js exists after install; pnpm why solid-js shows exactly one solid-js@2.0.0-beta.30 for solid-pacer; packages/pacer-devtools still resolves @tanstack/solid-store 0.11.0 from npm against solid-js 1.x.

title: Make @tanstack/solid-store git-installable in dkkloimwieder/store
description:
Two commits in /home/kaalin/dev/store (the user's own fork; not an upstream PR), then push and record the hash.

(a) packages/solid-store/package.json: change the dependency "@tanstack/store": "workspace:*" to "^0.11.0". pnpm only rewrites the workspace: protocol at pack/publish time, so a raw git checkout keeps the literal string and is unresolvable outside its own workspace. This is safe locally because that repo sets linkWorkspacePackages: true and preferWorkspacePackages: true, so ^0.11.0 still links to the workspace package.

(b) Un-ignore packages/solid-store/dist. .gitignore line 12 ignores dist repo-wide, and solid-store's exports map points only at ./dist/index.js and ./dist/index.cjs, so a clone currently has src/ but nothing importable. There is no prepare/prepack script, and adding one would not help: tsconfig.build.json extends ./tsconfig.json which extends ../../tsconfig.json, outside any #path: subdirectory extraction.

Build before committing dist (pnpm build in packages/solid-store).
acceptance_criteria: Both commits pushed to origin/main; git show <hash>:packages/solid-store/package.json shows ^0.11.0; git ls-files packages/solid-store/dist is non-empty; the new commit hash is recorded in this issue's notes.
notes: Pushed as 9709dab20a007c3e9dc2cd8cee0960d57e38cbea on origin/main (single commit, not two: the .gitignore un-ignore and the workspace:* -> ^0.11.0 change plus the lockfile specifier refresh and 52 dist files landed together). Verified before pushing: git check-ignore reports nothing for packages/solid-store/dist; the lockfile shows 'specifier: ^0.11.0 / version: link:../store', confirming the workspace link survives; pnpm build succeeded and all 46 solid-store tests pass.
close_reason: Store repo is git-installable; hash recorded in notes.

title: Solid 2: port the packages/solid-pacer adapter source
description:
Port the 32 files / 3,067 lines of packages/solid-pacer/src to SolidJS 2. The Solid-1-specific surface is small: no createComputed, onMount, splitProps, mergeProps, batch, observable, solid-js/store or solid-js/web anywhere in it.

The breakage inventory: 10x createEffect(() => onCleanup(...)) one-arg form; 3x createEffect(() => setX(value())) one-arg form; 1x <PacerContext.Provider>; 11 files importing the JSX type from solid-js; 3x createSignal<TValue>(value) against Solid 2's Exclude<T, Function> overload; 3x 'maybeExecute as Setter<TValue>' casts against Solid 2's invariant Setter<in out T>; 10x fragile 'return { ...instance, state }'.

Includes a latent defect fix: Throttler defaults leading:true and RateLimiter executes immediately under the limit, so createThrottledValue/createRateLimitedValue write a plain createSignal synchronously from inside an effect half, which is REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE under Solid 2.
acceptance_criteria: tsc, eslint (with the braced-effect-half rule) and tsdown+publint --strict all pass for packages/solid-pacer; no Solid 1 API remains in src; the public API surface (14 exported functions, 21 exported interfaces) is unchanged apart from the documented Solid 2 type changes.

title: Solid 2: toolchain, dependencies and workspace config
description:
Move packages/solid-pacer's dependency graph and build/test toolchain from Solid 1 to SolidJS 2 (2.0.0-beta.30). This is the blocking epic: nothing else can be verified until exactly one solid-js@2 runtime resolves for the adapter and its examples, and one Solid 1 tree remains for the devtools family.

Key facts: node_modules is NOT installed in this repo, so the first pnpm install re-resolves the whole graph. The real historical blocker was @tanstack/solid-store@0.11.0 from npm (peer solid-js ^1.6.0); it is resolved by consuming the migrated Solid 2 build from github.com/dkkloimwieder/store via a commit-pinned git dependency.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm install succeeds; pnpm why solid-js shows 2.0.0-beta.30 for solid-pacer + examples and only 1.9.x under the devtools family; pnpm why @solidjs/web shows a single copy; packages/solid-pacer/node_modules/@tanstack/solid-store/dist/index.js exists; sherif and knip pass.

title: Untrack the seeding read in the three create*Value wrappers
description:
Found by the browser pass (pacer-n8j.4). createDebouncedValue, createThrottledValue and createRateLimitedValue each seed their backing signal with a bare value() read in the component body. That read is owned and untracked, so Solid 2 emits [STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED] once per consumer — three warnings on the createThrottledValue example alone, one per App component.

It is a false positive rather than a staleness bug: the value keeps updating through the tracked createEffect below the seed. So the correct fix is a targeted untrack() at the seeding read only, matching solid-table's readSettled/untrack(signal) idiom — not a blanket suppression.
acceptance_criteria: untrack(value) at all three seeding reads; a regression test that FAILS without it; no STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED in the browser pass.
notes: Non-obvious: Solid 2 arms strict-read checking ONLY inside createComponent — solid-js/dist/dev.js devComponent() wraps the call as untrack(() => Comp(props), `<Name>`), and that second argument is the strictReadLabel. A test that renders the root callback directly (render(() => {...})) never arms it and passes vacuously. The test must render a real named component. The pre-existing diagnostics test in timing.test.tsx had this same defect and was silently unable to fail.

title: tsdown builds fail repo-wide: missing optional peer 'unrun'
description:
## Problem

Every tsdown build in the repo fails with:

    ERROR Error: Failed to import module "unrun". Please ensure it is installed.

tsdown 0.22.1 declares `unrun` as an OPTIONAL peerDependency and uses it to load the TypeScript `tsdown.config.ts`. pnpm does not auto-install optional peers, so the module is never present.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `pnpm install`
2. `cd packages/pacer && pnpm build`

Fails immediately, before any Solid code is involved.

## Pre-existing

NOT caused by the Solid 2 migration. Verified by reverting packageManager to pnpm@11.1.1 and restoring the committed pnpm-lock.yaml: `packages/pacer` fails identically. It reproduces on a pristine dependency graph.

## Fix

Added `unrun: ^0.3.0` to root devDependencies (resolves 0.3.1). `packages/pacer` then builds clean with publint reporting no issues.

Filed for visibility because it is an unrelated repo break that the Solid 2 branch now carries a fix for.
close_reason: Fixed by adding unrun ^0.3.0 to root devDependencies; packages/pacer and every other tsdown build now succeed.

title: Verify representative examples in a real browser
description:
This is where the port actually gets proven. tsc, eslint, tsdown+publint and even the unit suite are blind to most of what Solid 2 changes.

Run pnpm dev in a representative set covering every primitive family and both Subscribe children shapes: createDebouncer, createThrottledValue, createRateLimitedValue, createAsyncQueuer, createBatcher, createQueuedSignal, queue.

For each: no console errors, and specifically no REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE, no REACTIVITY_HALTED, and no unexplained STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED.

Behaviour to confirm:
- createDebouncer — Subscribe children update; status and executionCount advance; Flush works.
- createThrottledValue — the leading-edge write on first render succeeds. On an unfixed build this throws immediately; it is the direct browser check for the create*Signal defect.
- createRateLimitedValue — same, via the immediate-execute-under-limit path.
- createQueuedSignal and queue — items list tracks; devtools panel is gone and nothing errors.
- Unmount a component holding each primitive and confirm the cleanup matrix still fires.

On STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED: it is dev-build only and usually correct. Benign when the surrounding JSX tracks the same value by another path; a genuine staleness bug when a function reads a reactive value and returns a plain value. Do not blanket-untrack() it — the diagnostic is what discriminates.
acceptance_criteria: Every example in the set loads and behaves correctly with a clean console; findings recorded in this issue's notes.
notes:
DONE — verified in real Chrome 151 over CDP. The Claude-in-Chrome extension was never connected; /usr/bin/google-chrome plus node 22's global WebSocket made a zero-dependency CDP driver possible instead, which is better than a manual pass because it is reproducible. Committed as packages/solid-pacer/scripts/browser-verify (pnpm test:browser / test:browser:unmount), deliberately NOT in test:ci.

RESULTS: 87/87 checks across createDebouncer, createThrottledValue, createRateLimitedValue, createBatcher, createQueuedSignal, queue, createAsyncQueuer. Plus 23/23 unmount checks covering the full cleanup matrix for all 10 primitives in a live document. Input is dispatched through the CDP Input domain (trusted events), so event delegation is genuinely exercised.

CONFIRMED: the ownedWrite fix works. createThrottledValue mounts and its leading-edge write lands at first render; on an unfixed build that throws before paint. createRateLimitedValue likewise via the execute-immediately-under-limit path.

FOUND AND FIXED (pacer-cf9.10): all 3 create*Value wrappers seeded their backing signal with a bare value() read in the component body, emitting STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED once per consumer. False positive (the tracked effect keeps the value fresh), so fixed with a targeted untrack(value) matching solid-table's idiom.

FOUND AND FILED, NOT FIXED: pacer-dxw (core evaluates enabled() in the Debouncer constructor — benign, but packages/pacer is excluded by the plan's locked decisions) and pacer-n8j.5 (examples freeze windowType: windowType(), so the fixed/sliding radios genuinely do nothing — pre-existing upstream, and the diagnostic is CORRECT there so it must not be untracked away). Both are in verify.mjs's KNOWN allowlist with counts, so any new diagnostic still fails the run.

ALSO FOUND: STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED cannot be caught in jsdom unless the primitive is built inside a REAL component — Solid arms strict-read only in createComponent, whose dev wrapper is untrack(() => Comp(props), '<Name>'). The pre-existing diagnostics test in timing.test.tsx rendered a bare root callback and was therefore unable to fail. Both it and the new tests now render named components; verified by reverting the fix and watching the test go red.

title: Lowercase colSpan and rowSpan in example JSX
description:
Solid 2 requires the lowercase HTML attribute names colspan and rowspan; the React-style camelCase forms no longer map.

6 occurrences across 3 files:
  examples/solid/createDebouncer/src/index.tsx
  examples/solid/createDebouncedSignal/src/index.tsx
  examples/solid/createRateLimiter/src/index.tsx

All are <td colSpan={2}> separator rows inside the Subscribe tables.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Complete the example dependency sweep so the example builds against solid-js 2.0.0-beta.30 with jsxImportSource @solidjs/web.
2. Run pnpm dev in examples/solid/createDebouncer.
3. Inspect the separator row in the rendered table: the td does not span both columns, because colSpan is emitted as an unknown attribute rather than mapped to the colspan property.

## Fix
Rename colSpan to colspan (and rowSpan to rowspan, if any appear) in the three files, then grep repo-wide under examples/solid to confirm none remain.
acceptance_criteria: grep for colSpan/rowSpan under examples/solid returns nothing; the affected tables render with correct column spanning in a browser.
notes: colSpan was 6 sites across 3 files as planned. ALSO FOUND: a bare readOnly attribute in 14 of the 26 examples, which Solid 2 requires as lowercase readonly. It was invisible to the original survey because it is a valueless JSX attribute (no '=' to grep for) and it broke type-check in 14 examples, not 3. Swept both; a follow-up grep for the other common camelCase HTML attributes (maxLength, tabIndex, autoFocus, spellCheck, crossOrigin, contentEditable) found none.

title: Repoint the render import from solid-js/web to @solidjs/web
description:
All 26 examples/solid/*/src/index.tsx have 'import { render } from solid-js/web'. In Solid 2, solid-js has no ./web subpath — the DOM runtime moved to the separate @solidjs/web package, which exports render and the JSX type namespace (verified against @solidjs/web@2.0.0-beta.30).

This is the only solid-js/web usage in the examples. The other solid-js imports across all 26 are createSignal (26 files) and For (11 files), both of which survive Solid 2 unchanged and need no edit.
acceptance_criteria: No file under examples/solid/ imports from solid-js/web; all 26 examples type-check and render.

title: Sweep Solid 2 dependency and config pins across all 26 examples
description:
All 26 examples/solid/* are byte-identical in configuration, so this is one mechanical pass repeated 26 times.

package.json dependencies: solid-js and @solidjs/web at exactly 2.0.0-beta.30 (no caret — both the table and store repos pin exact on the Solid 2 side because of beta churn, and they bump in lockstep). devDependencies: vite-plugin-solid 3.0.0-next.21, vite stays ^8.0.12.

Note @solidjs/web goes in dependencies for an APP (unlike the library, where it is a peer).

tsconfig.json: jsxImportSource from solid-js to @solidjs/web. These tsconfigs are standalone and do not extend the root, and the line is at :15 in 25 of them and :16 in asyncBatch.

vite.config.ts needs no change in shape (plugins: [solid({})] still works); leave it.

Reference shape: /home/kaalin/dev/store/examples/solid/simple.
acceptance_criteria: All 26 package.json and tsconfig.json files updated; pnpm install resolves one solid-js@2.0.0-beta.30 across every example; each example's pnpm test:types passes.

title: Strip devtools wiring from the 3 Solid examples
description:
examples/solid/queue, examples/solid/createQueuer and examples/solid/createQueuedSignal each mount the devtools panel. Under Solid 2 this combination is not viable: @tanstack/solid-devtools is external and peer-only, so no package-manager config can give it a private Solid 1, and vite-plugin-solid@3 sets resolve.dedupe ['solid-js','@solidjs/web'] which enforces a Solid singleton by design. The table repo verified this end to end (bead table-rcv.7, NO-GO) and removed devtools from all 9 of its wired Solid examples rather than mixing runtimes.

Per example: drop the @tanstack/solid-devtools and @tanstack/solid-pacer-devtools dependencies, the two imports at the top of src/index.tsx, and the <TanStackDevtools plugins={[pacerDevtoolsPlugin()]}> block.

KEEP the key option where present — it is a real @tanstack/pacer API (pacerEventClient / emitChange), not devtools scaffolding. Update its comment to: // identifies this instance (used by TanStack Devtools when attached)
acceptance_criteria: No file under examples/solid/ imports or depends on any devtools package; the three examples build and run; the key option and its comment remain.

title: Cap solid-pacer-devtools peers below Solid 2
description:
packages/solid-pacer-devtools/package.json currently declares peerDependencies solid-js '>=1.9.7' and has no solid-js devDependency at all (it relies on an auto-installed peer).

Change the peer to '>=1.9.7 <2.0.0' and add solid-js ^1.9.14 to devDependencies.

The open-ended range matches nothing in the Solid 2 prerelease line today, but will match stable 2.0.0 the day it GAs — for a package whose entire dependency chain is built on APIs Solid 2 removed. The table repo made the same one-line change in commit 37f4e1af8 for exactly this reason.

Optionally align packages/pacer-devtools' solid-js dependency from ^1.9.12 to ^1.9.14 for consistency; it is already a hard dependency, which is the island-ready shape, so this is cosmetic.

Otherwise DO NOT touch either devtools package. The table repo changed zero source files in either of its two.
acceptance_criteria: solid-pacer-devtools peers are capped; its own build and tests still pass; no source file under packages/solid-pacer-devtools/src or packages/pacer-devtools/src is modified.

title: Pin the external devtools family's nested solid-js to 1.x
description:
Add scoped overrides to pnpm-workspace.yaml, one line per external devtools package:

  '@tanstack/devtools>solid-js': ^1.9.14
  '@tanstack/devtools-ui>solid-js': ^1.9.14
  '@tanstack/devtools-utils>solid-js': ^1.9.14
  '@tanstack/solid-devtools>solid-js': ^1.9.14
  '@tanstack/react-devtools>solid-js': ^1.9.14
  '@tanstack/preact-devtools>solid-js': ^1.9.14

Why: the TanStack devtools UI stack is built on Solid 1 and imports solid-js/web, an entrypoint solid-js@2 no longer exports. Once the Solid examples move to solid-js@2, pnpm's peer dedupe re-resolves this family against the workspace's Solid 2 and breaks the React and Preact devtools builds. That is the exact regression commit 066f57333 fixed in the table repo, where it took out five example builds.

CRITICAL: pnpm 11 IGNORES pnpm.overrides in package.json (warns 'field no longer read'). The root package.json here has no overrides block; pnpm-workspace.yaml does, and that is where these go.

Do NOT add an override for @tanstack/solid-store — see the sibling note on why that pin must stay in packages/solid-pacer/package.json.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm why solid-js shows 1.9.x under every devtools package and 2.0.0-beta.30 nowhere in that subtree; react-pacer-devtools and preact-pacer-devtools build with --skip-nx-cache.

title: Add per-primitive behaviour tests
description:
Coverage for what the type system cannot see:

- The Subscribe component renders and updates for each of the 10 primitives, with both children shapes (a function of the accessor, and plain JSX).
- A selector plus shallow compare suppresses an update when the selection is equal, and fires when it is not.
- The unmount matrix from the sibling issue: each primitive's default cleanup on owner disposal, plus the onUnmount override path.
- createQueuedSignal items tracking across add/remove/clear.
- The three create*Value mirrors, including leading:true for the debounced one.
- Disposal actually unsubscribes: assert the store has no listeners after disposal and that a post-disposal setState does not write.

Nested roots are parent-owned in Solid 2, so double-dispose is reachable — assert unsubscribe is idempotent.
acceptance_criteria: Suite covers all 16 exported primitives; test:lib green; coverage of src is meaningful rather than nominal.

title: Pin the Solid 2 timing contract
description:
Four assertions, each of which encodes observed runtime behaviour rather than design assumption:

1. Coalescing — N writes in one tick produce exactly one effect run per flush. This is what makes Solid 1's batch() unnecessary.
2. Consecutive functional updates in one tick see each other and compose.
3. Stale-window pin — an imperative read in the same synchronous tick as a store write returns the PREVIOUS value. Assert this explicitly so the deferral is a documented contract rather than an accident, and so a future settleOnRead change is a deliberate test edit.
4. Tracked reads are unaffected — the same value read from JSX or an effect compute half converges after a settle.

Note the store's own subscribe fires synchronously; it is Solid's graph that defers. Both halves matter.
acceptance_criteria: Four tests pass; the stale-window test carries a comment stating it must never gain a settle() between the write and the read.
close_reason: Timing contract pinned: stale same-tick read, coalescing, shallow-equal suppression. Plus a console-diagnostics guard that partially covers the blocked browser pass.

title: Add the effect-half return tripwire test
description:
A single-test file asserting that reactivity still works after an effect whose effect half returns a non-function value.

MUST be its own file with exactly one test. A REACTIVITY_HALTED failure poisons the entire module, so any sibling test in the same file becomes an unreliable false positive.

This is the executable counterpart to the ESLint rule: the rule catches the expression-bodied arrow syntactically, this catches the semantics if the rule is ever relaxed or bypassed.
acceptance_criteria: tests/unit/effect-cleanup-return.test.ts exists with one test; it passes; adding a deliberate violation makes it fail.

title: Create the Solid 2 test harness
description:
packages/solid-pacer/tests/ does not exist. Create:

- tests/utils/reactive.ts with settle() and createEffectTestRoot(), copied VERBATIM from /home/kaalin/dev/store/packages/solid-store/tests/utils/reactive.ts. settle() is just flush(); createEffectTestRoot runs setup inside a disposable root and returns [dispose, value].
- tests/test-setup.ts importing @testing-library/jest-dom/vitest (the repo already has that devDep, and solid-pacer-devtools/tests/test-setup.ts is the one-line template).

Rules that come with the harness, all learned from real failures:
- fireEvent NEVER flushes in Solid 2. Settle after every dispatch. Un-flushed read-modify-write handlers COLLAPSE across consecutive events — you get wrong values, not merely stale DOM.
- render() from @solidjs/testing-library is synchronous (it flushes internally).
- flush() THROWS inside onSettled or createTrackedEffect, and is a silent no-op inside an ordinary effect callback, so it cannot settle reads there either.
- Keep an explicit afterEach(cleanup) unless a global one is configured.
- One awaited microtask settles everything, so 'await Promise.resolve()' is a valid async settle.
acceptance_criteria: tests/utils/reactive.ts and tests/test-setup.ts exist; a trivial test using render + settle passes.

title: Verify createQueuedSignal under Solid 2 deferral
description:
packages/solid-pacer/src/queuer/createQueuedSignal.ts contains no Solid 1 API, so it needs no mechanical change — but it is the shape most exposed to Solid 2's update deferral and deserves verification rather than inspection.

It is the only primitive with a non-empty default selector, (state) => ({ items: state.items }), and it returns [() => queue.state().items, queue.addItem, queue]. The returned accessor reads through the useSelector signal at call time, so reads from JSX are tracked normally; the shallow comparator sees a new items array identity whenever the queuer replaces it.

What to confirm: that addItem followed by a tracked read settles to the new items, that the shallow compare does not suppress a legitimate update, and that an imperative read in the same tick is stale in the documented way rather than in a surprising one.
acceptance_criteria: A test covers add/remove/clear driving the items accessor from JSX, plus an explicit assertion of the same-tick stale read.

title: Preserve the per-primitive unmount matrix
description:
Easy to flatten accidentally while refactoring the 10 primitives. The current defaults, when no onUnmount option is supplied, are deliberately NOT uniform:

  createDebouncer        -> cancel()
  createThrottler        -> cancel()
  createBatcher          -> cancel()
  createQueuer           -> stop()
  createRateLimiter      -> NO default cleanup at all (only calls onUnmount if provided; no else branch)
  createAsyncDebouncer   -> cancel(); abort()
  createAsyncThrottler   -> cancel(); abort()
  createAsyncBatcher     -> cancel(); abort()
  createAsyncQueuer      -> stop(); abort()
  createAsyncRateLimiter -> abort()

Keep every one exactly as it is, including createRateLimiter's missing default — changing it is a behaviour change that belongs in its own issue, not smuggled into a framework port.
acceptance_criteria: A test pins all 10 cleanup behaviours; createRateLimiter still performs no default cleanup.

title: Harden the returned instance shape in the 10 store-backed primitives
description:
Each primitive ends with 'return { ...instance, state } as SolidX<...>'. Spreading a live class instance copies own enumerable properties only — prototype methods and prototype getters are dropped.

It works TODAY only by luck: every @tanstack/pacer class (Debouncer, Throttler, Batcher, Queuer, RateLimiter and the async five) defines all its methods as arrow class fields, with no prototype methods and no getters anywhere in the core — verified. The moment a core method moves to the prototype, every Solid primitive silently loses it. The equivalent bug bit the table adapter twice.

Replace with an attach-and-return:
  Object.defineProperty(instance, 'state', { get: () => state, enumerable: true })
  return instance as SolidX<TFn, TSelected>

Note the current code claims to omit 'store' in favour of 'state' but the spread actually copies it, and the SolidX interface declares both. Preserve the existing observable behaviour; do not change the public shape here.
acceptance_criteria: All 10 primitives return an object exposing every instance method plus a reactive state accessor; behaviour is unchanged for consumers; a test asserts a prototype-defined method would survive.

title: Unblock sherif for the mixed solid-js workspace
description:
Root package.json test:sherif runs bare with zero config — there is no sherif.json anywhere in the repo, so all default rules are active at error severity, including multiple-dependency-versions.

solid-js is currently uniform at ^1.9.12 across packages/solid-pacer, packages/pacer-devtools and all 26 examples/solid/*. Bumping only the adapter and its examples to 2.0.0-beta.30 makes sherif fail immediately. Same for vite-plugin-solid (2.x for devtools, 3.0.0-next.21 for the Solid 2 line).

Mirror the table repo exactly:
  "test:sherif": "sherif --ignore-dependency solid-js --ignore-dependency vite-plugin-solid"

If sherif's unsync-similar-dependencies heuristic pairs solid-js with @solidjs/web, add --ignore-rule unsync-similar-dependencies. It did not fire in the table repo, so try without it first.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm test:sherif passes with solid-js at two major versions in the workspace.

title: Add packageExtensions for @solidjs/testing-library and vite-plugin-solid peers
description:
pnpm-workspace.yaml has no packageExtensions block today; add one.

@solidjs/testing-library@1.0.0-beta.2 declares peers of >=2.0.0 for both solid-js and @solidjs/web. Semver admits a prerelease only when some comparator in the range shares its major.minor.patch, so >=2.0.0 does not match 2.0.0-beta.30 and the peers are unsatisfiable. Relax both to '>=2.0.0-0 <3.0.0'.

vite-plugin-solid 3.0.0-next.21 has not widened its @testing-library/jest-dom peer to ^7, which the repo root carries. Widen it to '^5.16.6 || ^6.0.0 || ^7.0.0'.

Both are transition-only and get removed at Solid 2 GA (tracked separately).

CRITICAL: pnpm 11 silently IGNORES pnpm.packageExtensions and pnpm.overrides in package.json — it warns 'field no longer read'. These must live in pnpm-workspace.yaml or they do nothing.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm install completes with no unsatisfiable-peer errors for @solidjs/testing-library or vite-plugin-solid.
notes: Implemented as packageExtensions in pnpm-workspace.yaml (not peerDependencyRules), mirroring the table repo. IMPORTANT DEVIATION: this required bumping packageManager from pnpm@11.1.1 to pnpm@11.18.0. pnpm 11.1.1 silently ignores packageExtensions in pnpm-workspace.yaml entirely — it never writes a packageExtensionsChecksum and changes to the block do not invalidate the lockfile. It also does not apply scoped '>solid-js' overrides to peer resolution, which is what pacer-fsq.1 depends on. Verified the bump is safe: the pre-existing packages/pacer build failure (missing 'unrun', see pacer-frf) reproduces identically on 11.1.1 with the committed lockfile, so it is not a consequence of the bump; and all four devtools adapters plus the five React/Preact devtools examples build clean afterwards. pnpm 11.18.0 also adds a minimum-release-age supply-chain policy that rejects the day-old Solid 2 betas, so a minimumReleaseAgeExclude block was added alongside.

title: Solid 2: migrate the 26 Solid examples
description:
All 26 examples/solid/* dirs are byte-identical in configuration (standalone tsconfig, identical vite.config.ts, same dependency block). The migration is a mechanical sweep plus three specific code fixes.

Verified surface: 'import { render } from solid-js/web' in all 26 src/index.tsx (solid-js has no ./web subpath in Solid 2); createSignal in all 26 and For in 11 (both survive unchanged); 6 colSpan/rowSpan attributes across 3 files that Solid 2 requires lowercase; 3 examples wire devtools.

The examples are the only end-to-end proof the adapter works in a browser.
acceptance_criteria: all 26 examples type-check; a representative set runs in a real browser with no console errors and specifically no REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE, REACTIVITY_HALTED or unexplained STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED.
close_reason: All 5 children complete. Acceptance met: all 26 examples type-check; a representative set was driven in real Chrome at 87/87 checks with no REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE, no REACTIVITY_HALTED, and the only remaining STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED (2, from createDebouncer) now explained and recorded under pacer-dxw -> pacer-avi rather than unexplained.

title: Solid 2: quarantine the devtools stack on Solid 1
description:
Mirror what dkkloimwieder/table did. A Solid 1 devtools island inside a Solid 2 app was spiked there (bead table-rcv.7) and closed NO-GO, runtime-verified at three layers: packageExtensions cannot retarget a peer-declared solid-js for an external package; vite-plugin-solid@3 sets resolve.dedupe ['solid-js','@solidjs/web'] and enforces a Solid singleton by design; and even a bespoke per-importer resolveId plugin left the panel unmounted, leaked cross-runtime computations and once hit REACTIVITY_HALTED, killing the host app.

So devtools get quarantined, not mixed: 0 of 36 Solid examples there reference devtools, while all 51 React/Preact/Vue/Angular devtools examples keep working on a nested, never-hoisted Solid 1.

packages/pacer-devtools already declares solid-js ^1.9.12 as a hard dependency (the island-ready shape table had to create deliberately). The only non-viable combination here is the 3 Solid examples mounting @tanstack/solid-devtools, an external peer-only package.
acceptance_criteria: react-pacer-devtools and preact-pacer-devtools still build with --skip-nx-cache; no Solid example depends on any devtools package; solid-pacer-devtools peers are capped <2.0.0; packages/pacer-devtools source is unmodified.

title: Solid 2: build a test suite for solid-pacer from zero
description:
packages/solid-pacer has NO tests today: test:lib is 'vitest --passWithNoTests', vitest.config.ts points at a ./tests directory that does not exist, and its setupFiles line is commented out. Every gate that exists (tsc, eslint, tsdown+publint) is blind to the semantic regressions this port is prone to — owned-scope writes, effect-half return values, update deferral, cleanup behaviour.

A test suite is therefore part of the port, not a follow-up. Harness copied verbatim from /home/kaalin/dev/store/packages/solid-store/tests/utils/reactive.ts.
acceptance_criteria: tests/ exists with a working harness; test:lib runs real tests (no --passWithNoTests); the owned-scope-write regression, the effect-half return tripwire, the timing contract and the per-primitive unmount matrix are all pinned; suite is green.
close_reason: All six children closed; 47 tests where there were none.

title: solid-pacer and angular-pacer publish a stale status for function-form enabled
description:
Found while investigating pacer-dxw; reproduced with tests now committed in packages/solid-pacer/tests/optionReactivity.test.tsx.

THE DEFECT
'status' is derived state, computed only inside each core class's private #setState. Debouncer.maybeExecute (packages/pacer/src/debouncer.ts:222) early-returns BEFORE reaching #setState when disabled; AsyncDebouncer (async-debouncer.ts:321) and AsyncThrottler (async-throttler.ts:341) do the same. And grep -rn setOptions packages/solid-pacer/src returns ZERO matches — likewise packages/angular-pacer/src. So once a function-form 'enabled' flips false, nothing ever recomputes status and the adapter keeps publishing the previous value indefinitely.

MEASURED (solid-js 2.0.0-beta.30, jsdom):
  enabled: () => n() > 2, starting n=5
  maybeExecute()      -> status 'pending'   (correct)
  setN(0)             -> status 'pending'   (STALE, should be 'disabled')
  maybeExecute()      -> status 'pending'   (still stale — early return)

RateLimiter is unaffected: its maybeExecute writes state before gating (rate-limiter.ts:252-255), so status recovers to 'disabled'.

WHY REACT AND PREACT DO NOT HAVE IT
Their hooks call instance.setOptions(mergedOptions) on every render (react-pacer/src/debouncer/useDebouncer.ts:195, preact equivalent), and setOptions calls cancel() when disabled, which writes state. Solid component bodies run once and Angular's injectors likewise, so neither ever pushes.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND COSMETICS
This is what Solid 2's [STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED] on the constructor's enabled read is actually reporting. Its message — 'Reactive value read directly in <Comp> will not update' — is literally true of the status this adapter publishes. See pacer-dxw for why that diagnostic is therefore being ACCEPTED rather than untracked away.

CANDIDATE FIXES, NEITHER YET SAFE
(a) Adapter-side effect pushing setOptions. Measured: repairs the disable direction but NOT re-enable, because setOptions only writes state via cancel() when it becomes disabled — going enabled again sets options with no state write. Half a fix.
(b) Core: make setOptions always recompute derived state. HAZARD TO CHECK FIRST — react-pacer calls setOptions on EVERY render, and #setState always allocates a fresh state object, so an unconditional recompute risks a render/notify/render loop in React. Verify against react-pacer's useStore compare before attempting.

A real fix likely needs both, plus a decision about whether Solid should accept accessor-form options the way react-pacer accepts a fresh object per render.
acceptance_criteria: A function-form enabled keeps status accurate in solid-pacer, or the limitation is documented in the adapter's JSDoc and the characterisation test updated.
close_reason:
FIXED in solid-pacer (angular tracked separately as pacer-vee, out of scope here).

WHAT CHANGED — packages/solid-pacer only, 3 files:
createDebouncer, createAsyncDebouncer, createAsyncThrottler each gained:
  const enabled = createMemo(() => parseFunctionOrValue(instance.options.enabled, instance))
  createEffect(() => enabled(), (_next, prev) => { if (prev !== undefined) instance.cancel() })

WHY THAT SHAPE, all measured rather than reasoned:
- cancel() is the ONLY public core call that writes state unconditionally (debouncer.ts:285-291), and a state write is what forces the derived status to be recomputed. On the disabling edge it is also exactly what core setOptions does (debouncer.ts:179), so this does not invent behaviour — it aligns Solid with React's effective disable semantics, which additionally means a pending debounce is now genuinely cancelled on disable rather than left running.
- The createMemo is load-bearing. MEASURED: a bare two-arg createEffect re-runs its effect half on every dependency change, not only when the computed value flips — [false,false,true,true,true] for five writes to the underlying signal, vs [false,true] when memo-wrapped. Without it, an 'enabled: () => q().length > 2' would cancel() on every keystroke and destroy the very debounce whose status it reports. Pinned by the test 'does not disturb a pending debounce while enabled stays true'.
- prev === undefined identifies the mount run (measured); skipping it leaves a caller-supplied initialState intact and is safe because the constructor already computed status correctly.

SCOPE OF THE DEFECT — verified across all 10 core classes, only 3 are affected: Debouncer (debouncer.ts:222), AsyncDebouncer (async-debouncer.ts:321), AsyncThrottler (async-throttler.ts:341) gate at the top of maybeExecute before any #setState. Sync Throttler and both rate limiters write state FIRST and gate later, so they self-heal. Queuers and batchers have no disabled status at all.

NO CORE CHANGE. The core-side option (making setOptions always recompute) was dropped as out of scope — packages/pacer is shared by every adapter, so it could not be changed without affecting react/preact.

TESTS: packages/solid-pacer/tests/optionReactivity.test.tsx, 4 -> 8 tests. The characterisation test that pinned the stale behaviour now asserts the correct behaviour. EVERY new assertion was proven able to fail by reverting the corresponding guard: disabling the fix failed both status tests ('pending' != 'disabled', 'disabled' != 'idle'); removing only the memo failed the keystroke test ('idle' != 'pending'); disabling the async fixes failed both parametrised async tests.

GATES: nx test:types/test:eslint/test:lib/build across solid-pacer + solid-pacer-devtools with --skip-nx-cache; 58 tests; sherif; knip; SSR dist gate (64 files); react+preact devtools builds; all 26 Solid examples type-check.

title: Rate-limiter examples freeze windowType, so the fixed/sliding radios do nothing
description:
Found by the browser pass (pacer-n8j.4); pre-existing upstream, not caused by the Solid 2 port, but newly surfaced by Solid 2's STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED diagnostic.

examples/solid/createRateLimitedValue (App1/App2/App3), createRateLimitedSignal and createRateLimiter all build their options as:

    { limit: 5, window: 5000, windowType: windowType() }

windowType() is a createSignal read evaluated once, in the component body, when the options object literal is constructed — before the adapter is even called. The value is then frozen into the instance. Clicking the Fixed/Sliding radios updates the signal and re-renders the radio, but the rate limiter keeps its original windowType forever.

Confirmed by stack trace in Chrome: the read is attributed to App1/App2/App3 in the example's own src/index.tsx, not to solid-pacer.

Cannot be fixed by passing a function: RateLimiterOptions.windowType is typed 'fixed' | 'sliding' with no function form (packages/pacer/src/rate-limiter.ts:86), and the Solid adapter never calls setOptions. A real fix needs an effect calling rateLimiter.setOptions({ windowType }) — a behaviour change beyond the scope of the Solid 2 port, so filed rather than fixed.

Do NOT silence this with untrack(): here the diagnostic is correct — the value really is stale.
acceptance_criteria: Either the radios drive setOptions, or the option is removed from the examples.
notes:
FIXED. 14 frozen windowType sites across 6 example files (the bead recorded 3 files; a full survey of all 26 examples found 6).

GROUP A — 10 components across 4 files (createRateLimiter x3, createAsyncRateLimiter x1, createRateLimitedSignal x3, createRateLimitedValue x3): removed 'windowType: windowType()' from the construction-time options literal and added a two-arg createEffect pushing it through setOptions. The effect half also runs at mount, so the initial 'fixed' is applied and the option can leave the literal entirely — the stale read is removed at its source rather than untracked away, as the bead required. Two createRateLimitedValue call sites had to widen their destructure to expose the instance.

GROUP B — 4 components across 2 files (rateLimit x3, asyncRateLimit x1): rateLimit()/asyncRateLimit() return only the bound maybeExecute, so there is no instance and setOptions is impossible. Took the second acceptance branch: removed the dead radios and added a comment pointing at createRateLimiter. NOTE: React's examples/react/rateLimit keeps its toggle via useCallback(...,[windowType]) and its own comment calls that a workaround ('consider using useRateLimiter instead'). Filed pacer-rcz so the Solid/React divergence is not silent.

ALSO FOLDED IN (same files, same root cause):
- createRateLimitedSignal passed a bare signal read as the positional seed at 3 sites; replaced with the literal the signal was created with. Without this, 3 of the 10 Group A components stayed diagnostic-dirty.
- createRateLimiter App2 froze 'enabled: instantSearch().length > 2' to false at construction, so that example was dead from page load. Converted to function form. It now gates one keystroke late (Solid 2 defers signal writes, so the read inside maybeExecute sees the previous value) — matching the React example; noted in a comment.

VERIFIED: all 26 examples type-check; prettier clean; browser harness 87/87 with the createRateLimitedValue STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED allowance REMOVED from KNOWN (was 3, now 0, confirmed in real Chrome). New test packages/solid-pacer/tests/optionReactivity.test.tsx pins the effect->setOptions idiom as diagnostic-clean and asserts the option actually flips.

title: Core evaluates enabled() eagerly in the constructor, tripping STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED
description:
Found by the browser pass (pacer-n8j.4), stack-traced in real Chrome.

Debouncer's constructor calls #setState(initialState), which computes status via #getEnabled() -> parseFunctionOrValue(this.options.enabled). When a Solid consumer passes 'enabled: () => someSignal() > 2' — as examples/solid/createDebouncer App1 and App2 do — that user function runs synchronously inside the mounting component, where Solid 2 has strict-read checking armed. Result: [STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED] once per instance.

Stack (packages/pacer/dist):
  enabled (examples/solid/createDebouncer/src/index.tsx:253)
  parseFunctionOrValue (utils.js:6)
  Debouncer.#getEnabled (debouncer.js:87)
  debouncer.js:81  <- from the constructor

BENIGN, not a staleness bug: #getEnabled is re-evaluated on every maybeExecute, and the browser pass confirms the enable/disable gate works correctly at runtime. It is console noise only — but it fires for every Solid consumer using a signal-reading option function.

OUT OF SCOPE for the Solid 2 port: the fix belongs in packages/pacer (framework-agnostic core), which the migration plan's locked decisions explicitly exclude from modification. Do NOT 'fix' this by untracking construction in the Solid adapter — that would blanket-suppress genuinely stale option reads such as 'wait: someSignal()', which the diagnostic correctly catches.
acceptance_criteria: Either the core defers the initial enabled evaluation, or a decision is recorded that the warning is accepted.
notes:
DECISION RECORDED — the warning is ACCEPTED (second acceptance branch). Both 'fix' options are worse than the status quo, and the premise in this bead's own description turned out to be wrong.

1. THE DIAGNOSTIC IS A TRUE POSITIVE, NOT BENIGN. This bead called it 'BENIGN, not a staleness bug'. That is incorrect. 'status' is derived only inside #setState; Debouncer/AsyncDebouncer/AsyncThrottler maybeExecute early-return before #setState when disabled; and solid-pacer never calls setOptions. Measured: with enabled: () => n() > 2 starting at n=5, status goes 'pending', then setN(0) leaves it 'pending', and a further maybeExecute leaves it 'pending' — permanently stale. Solid's message 'will not update' is literally accurate for the value this adapter publishes. Filed as pacer-avi with the repro; pinned by a characterisation test in packages/solid-pacer/tests/optionReactivity.test.tsx.

2. UNTRACKING CONSTRUCTION IN THE ADAPTER — REJECTED. Mechanically it works (measured: 1 diagnostic -> 0), and this bead's stated reason for rejecting it was ALSO wrong: an untrack inside the adapter cannot mask a genuinely stale 'wait: someSignal()', because the caller's options literal is evaluated before the adapter is entered (measured — that read still fires through an untracking adapter). But it is rejected on the stronger ground that it would silence the only automated signal of the pacer-avi defect.

3. CORE-DEFERRING THE INITIAL EVALUATION — REJECTED, actively harmful. Because maybeExecute early-returns before #setState and Solid/Angular never call setOptions, a deferred initial evaluation would leave status at 'idle' for the ENTIRE disabled period, not merely at first paint. React and Preact would self-heal via their per-render setOptions, so the regression would be invisible in the React examples and permanent in the Solid ones. It would also break packages/pacer/tests/async-retryer.test.ts:447 and :937, which assert 'disabled' immediately after construction (both use a plain boolean enabled: false, so a function-only defer would instead make enabled: false and enabled: () => false disagree about initial status).

SCOPE NOTE: the constructor's read surface is wider than this bead recorded. Instrumenting Debouncer showed it invokes exactly ['enabled'], but RateLimiter's #setState also calls #getLimit(), and its constructor runs #getExecutionTimesInWindow()/#setCleanupTimeout() which read windowType and window; the queuers invoke getPriority/getIsExpired and the user's fn when initialItems is supplied.

NET: packages/pacer is unchanged. The browser harness continues to allow exactly 2 STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED from createDebouncer, cited to this bead.
close_reason: Warning accepted; it is a true positive pointing at pacer-avi. Both fix options proven harmful.

title: Write the changeset for the breaking peer change
description:
Dropping Solid 1 support is a major/breaking change for @tanstack/solid-pacer: the peer range moves from '>=1.9.5' to '>=2.0.0-beta.30 <3.0.0' and @solidjs/web becomes a required peer.

.changeset/ currently contains only config.json — there are no pending changesets. Note the repo's changeset config sets onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange: true and baseBranch main, and release.yml publishes from main, alpha, beta and rc. A Solid 2 port is a natural fit for the beta channel if it is ever released, but no release or PR is in scope here.

Include @tanstack/solid-pacer-devtools if its peer cap counts as breaking for consumers.
acceptance_criteria: A changeset file exists describing the Solid 2 requirement and the dropped Solid 1 support; pnpm changeset status is clean.

title: Add the SSR-safety dist gate
description:
Port /home/kaalin/dev/store/packages/solid-store/scripts/check-ssr-safe-dist.mjs into packages/solid-pacer/scripts/ and wire it into a new test:build script alongside publint --strict.

Why it earns its place: @solidjs/web's server build replaces client-only exports with stubs that throw ON CALL, not on import. So an accidental client-only import fails neither the build nor the browser tests — it fails at runtime, under SSR, in a consumer's app. Nothing else in the gate matrix catches it.

solid-pacer compiles exactly one JSX site (the <PacerContext value> provider in PacerProvider.tsx), so the expected @solidjs/web import surface is tiny — createComponent and memo, the same allowlist the store repo uses. Any growth in that surface is worth a deliberate look rather than an automatic allow.

Also note packages/preact-pacer already has a test:build script running publint --strict; solid-pacer currently relies on tsdown's built-in publint instead.
acceptance_criteria: test:build script exists and passes; deliberately importing a client-only @solidjs/web symbol makes it fail.

title: Run the full gate matrix with the nx cache skipped
description:
Use --skip-nx-cache throughout: nx caching masked exactly this class of breakage for a full commit range in the table repo.

  nx run-many -t test:types,test:eslint,test:lib,build --projects=packages/solid-pacer,packages/solid-pacer-devtools --skip-nx-cache
  pnpm test:sherif
  pnpm test:knip
  nx run-many -t build --projects=packages/react-pacer-devtools,packages/preact-pacer-devtools --skip-nx-cache
  for d in examples/solid/*/; do (cd "$d" && pnpm test:types) || echo "FAIL $d"; done

The react/preact devtools build is not incidental — it is the direct check that the scoped solid-js overrides did their job. Note root test:pr uses nx affected, and touching pnpm-workspace.yaml, root package.json or tsconfig.json invalidates every project's cache via the sharedGlobals named input, so expect a full-repo rebuild.
acceptance_criteria: All commands green; no peer warnings for solid-js or @solidjs/web; all 26 examples type-check.
notes: Re-verified 2026-08-03 AFTER the browser pass and the create*Value untrack fix (commit 38f96934), all with --skip-nx-cache: nx matrix over solid-pacer + solid-pacer-devtools (test:types, test:eslint, test:lib, build) green; 50 vitest tests pass; sherif clean; knip clean (needed a packages/solid-pacer entry ignoring scripts/browser-verify/unmount-app, which is browser-loaded via index.html and so unreachable from the module graph); SSR dist gate reports 64 files with no unsafe @solidjs/web imports; react-pacer-devtools and preact-pacer-devtools both build, which is the direct proof the scoped solid-js overrides still pin the devtools family to Solid 1; all 26 Solid examples type-check.

title: Watch for @solidjs/web phantom-peer ambiguity
description:
Diagnostic issue — close as not-needed if it never fires.

Once two @solidjs/web peer variants exist in one workspace (one bound to solid-js 1 via the devtools family, one to solid-js 2), pnpm's hoisted fallback becomes ambiguous for any package that imports @solidjs/web without declaring it as a dependency or peer. The symptom is a MISSING_EXPORT at build time in a package you did not touch.

The table repo hit this with @tanstack/solid-query and fixed it with a packageExtensions entry declaring the peer:
  '@tanstack/solid-query':
    peerDependencies:
      '@solidjs/web': '>=2.0.0-0 <3.0.0'

If it fires here, identify the offending package from the build error and add the equivalent entry to pnpm-workspace.yaml.
acceptance_criteria: Either no MISSING_EXPORT occurs across a full --skip-nx-cache build (close as not needed), or a packageExtensions entry resolves it.
close_reason: Did not fire. The @solidjs/web phantom-peer ambiguity never surfaced: solid-pacer declares the peer explicitly and all four devtools adapters plus the five React/Preact devtools examples build clean. Reopen if a MISSING_EXPORT appears.

title: Recover devtools smoke coverage lost with the examples
description:
Stripping the three examples removes the only runtime exercise of the Solid devtools panel. packages/solid-pacer-devtools/tests/ currently holds index.test.ts (an 'expect(true).toBe(true)' placeholder) and panel-props.test.tsx (asserts raw JSX truthiness) — neither renders anything.

Add a Solid 1 jsdom render smoke test to that package, as the table repo did in commit 8fd8a771f. Its own devDeps keep Solid 1 under pnpm isolation, so it runs against the correct runtime.

Import the real modules directly rather than through the barrel: the barrel NoOps outside NODE_ENV=development, so a barrel import would assert nothing.
acceptance_criteria: A test renders the devtools panel under Solid 1 in jsdom and asserts real DOM output; packages/solid-pacer-devtools test:lib passes.

title: Fix the stale vitest.workspace.js project paths
description:
Root vitest.workspace.js lists './packages/solid-pacer/vite.config.ts' and './packages/react-pacer/vite.config.ts'. Neither file has ever existed — every package in this repo uses vitest.config.ts. Nothing in package.json scripts invokes the workspace file (tests run via nx affected --targets=test:lib into per-package vitest), so this has been dead config.

Worth fixing now that solid-pacer actually has tests. Root tsconfig.json explicitly includes vitest.workspace.js, so knip may also be surfacing the unresolved imports.

title: Document the settleOnRead policy on the state accessor
description:
Decision (locked at planning): leave settleOnRead OFF, matching the default the dkkloimwieder/store migration chose.

Rationale: diverging would make the two adapters disagree about the same primitive; every read in the 26 examples and in the Subscribe component is a tracked JSX read, unaffected either way; and the JSDoc's 'const { isPending } = debouncer.state()' pattern is an owned component-body read, where useSelector's guard correctly declines to flush regardless.

So this issue is documentation, not code: add a note to the SolidX.state JSDoc in each of the 10 primitives saying that reads from JSX, memos and effects are tracked as usual, while an imperative read in the same synchronous tick as a state change returns the previous value because Solid 2 settles on a microtask.

If the policy is ever reversed, it is one added option at the 20 useSelector call sites plus flipping the stale-window test assertion.
acceptance_criteria: All 10 SolidX.state JSDoc blocks carry the deferral note; no useSelector call site passes settleOnRead.
close_reason: Documented the deferral contract and the settleOnRead decision on the state accessor in all 10 primitives.

title: Add a knip workspace entry for packages/solid-pacer
description:
knip.json has entries for react-pacer, react-pacer-devtools, preact-pacer-devtools and solid-pacer-devtools but none for solid-pacer, so it is fully checked. The new devDependencies (@solidjs/web, @solidjs/testing-library) and the changed @tanstack/solid-store spec will surface as unused or unlisted.

Note @solidjs/web is imported directly by the source (the JSX type import and the compiled JSX runtime), so it may need no ignore at all — the table repo added a knip ignore for it and then removed it again for exactly that reason. Add the entry only for what actually fires; do not pre-emptively silence.

examples/** is already covered by ignoreWorkspaces.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm test:knip passes.
close_reason: No knip entry needed. knip passes clean against the new devDependencies (@solidjs/web, @solidjs/testing-library, jsdom) with no configuration. Per the bead's own guidance, not pre-emptively silencing.

title: Other adapters carry the same stale-status defect (angular both edges, react/preact re-enable edge)
description:
Filed while fixing pacer-avi in solid-pacer. OUT OF SCOPE to fix under the standing 'do not touch other framework adapters' instruction — recorded so it is not lost.

ANGULAR (both edges, same as Solid was):
grep -rn setOptions packages/angular-pacer/src returns nothing, and an Angular injector body runs once, so a function-form 'enabled' leaves the derived 'status' frozen at its constructed value in exactly the three primitives Solid had it in: Debouncer (packages/pacer/src/debouncer.ts:222), AsyncDebouncer (async-debouncer.ts:321), AsyncThrottler (async-throttler.ts:341) — the three whose maybeExecute gates before reaching #setState.

REACT / PREACT (re-enable edge only):
these call instance.setOptions(mergedOptions) every render (react-pacer/src/debouncer/useDebouncer.ts:195), and core setOptions writes state only via cancel() on the DISABLING branch (debouncer.ts:179). The enabling branch writes nothing, so status stays 'disabled' after enabled flips back true until some other state write happens. Not verified by a running test — inferred from the source and worth measuring before acting.

THE SOLID FIX, for reference (packages/solid-pacer, commit on this branch):
a createMemo over parseFunctionOrValue(instance.options.enabled, instance), plus a two-arg createEffect whose effect half calls instance.cancel() on every transition after mount. cancel() is the only public core call that writes state unconditionally, which is what forces the recompute. The memo is load-bearing — measured, a bare two-arg createEffect re-runs its effect half on every dependency change ([false,false,true,true,true] for five writes), which would cancel a pending debounce on every keystroke.
acceptance_criteria: Either the other adapters are fixed the same way, or a decision is recorded that they stay as-is.

title: Solid rateLimit examples: record why the windowType control was removed
description:
SCOPE: packages/solid-pacer and examples/solid ONLY. Other frameworks are permanently out of scope — do not read this issue as licence to edit examples/react or any other adapter's examples.

pacer-n8j.5 removed the dead Fixed/Sliding radios from examples/solid/rateLimit (3 components) and examples/solid/asyncRateLimit (1). The removal was correct: rateLimit()/asyncRateLimit() return only the bound maybeExecute, so there is no instance to call setOptions on and the radios could never have worked. The Solid examples already carry an explanatory comment pointing readers at createRateLimiter, which has a live toggle driven through setOptions.

Remaining work, if any, is Solid-side only: decide whether that comment is sufficient or whether the Solid examples should demonstrate a createMemo-based recreation pattern. Doing nothing is an acceptable outcome.
acceptance_criteria: Either the Solid examples gain a recreation demo, or a decision is recorded that the existing comment is sufficient. No non-Solid files are touched.

title: Follow-up: refresh the Solid docs left stale by this port
description:
Deliberately out of scope for this port by instruction, filed rather than silently dropped.

docs/framework/solid/adapter.md (284 lines, hand-written) still shows Solid 1 usage including 'import { createSignal } from solid-js' at :24, and says nothing about the Solid 2 requirement, the update-deferral timing contract, or the removal of devtools from the examples.

docs/framework/solid/reference/** (43 files: 20 functions, 22 interfaces, 1 index) is typedoc output generated by scripts/generate-docs.ts from packages/solid-pacer/src JSDoc via tsconfig.docs.json. It regenerates automatically — .github/workflows/autofix.yml runs 'pnpm build:all && pnpm generate-docs' on every PR and auto-commits the diff. Since no PR is being opened, it will simply stay stale until someone runs pnpm generate-docs.

Worth considering when actioned: a Solid 2 guide page modelled on the table repo's docs/framework/solid/guide/solid-2.md, covering the timing contract, STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED and the devtools situation. Also note docs/config.json must stay in lockstep with examples/solid/* directory names — scripts/check-missing-docs.sh cross-checks this and is not wired into any npm script.
acceptance_criteria: Not actionable during this port. Close when the docs are updated or when a decision is made to leave them.
